correctness.rationale: Exact independence-set split gives I(H∘overline(K_m),z)=(1+z)^(mn) I(H,z/(1+z)^m) and, when core roots are -a_j<=-1/4, factors as (1+z)^(m(n-alpha)) times ∏(z+a_j(1+z)^m)/∏a_j. For each m>=1,a>=1/4, roots of (1+z)^m+z/a begin close to -1 for a large and cannot cross the imaginary axis: z=iy (y>0) forces mθ=3π/2+2πk and a=sinθ cos^(m-1)θ. m<=3 admits no such phase; for m=4..6 the first admissible angle yields a<1/4; for m>=7 the GLOBAL maximum (m-1)^((m-1)/2)/m^(m/2)<=sqrt(6^6/7^7)<1/4 excludes all crossings. Conjugation handles negative y; zero is not a root. Path and cycle recurrence supplies exactly real roots -1/(4cos² θ)<-1/4 for all allowed orders. Independent approximate roots for 75 (m,a) scalar factors and exact elementary inequalities corroborate, not replace, the continuity proof.
residual_risks: Condition is sufficient not necessary; no optimality claimed for a=1/4 or nonuniform leaf counts.

The spider paper was only accessible by abstract; OAuth/Oxford returned VPN disconnected. Unknown more general stability theorem remains risk.

Uniform all-m root-barrier transfer to infinite multi-branch stable families
value.rationale: Strict stability of independence polynomials is an active graph-polynomial problem with counterexamples among trees. This root-geometric sufficient condition transfers a simple quantitative core-root barrier into infinite stable caterpillar families with arbitrarily many branching vertices and non-tree cycle coronas, all leaf multiplicities m>=2. The scalar half-plane no-crossing argument is a reusable structural mechanism and exceeds the existing spider family; one does not rely on the old whiskering identity alone.
residual_risks: No classification of all stable trees, no nonuniform leaves and no sharp optimal scalar barrier claimed.

limitations: Condition is sufficient not necessary; no optimality claimed for a=1/4 or nonuniform leaf counts.
